newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wine levy seen boosting overseas push.
newsitem.headline: Australian wine levy seen boosting overseas push.

text.p: International marketing of Australian wines would be boosted by the imposition of a value-based levy on exports, the Winemakers' Federation of Australia said on Monday.

Federation president Stephen Shelmerdine said the funds raised by the levy would guarantee the infrastructure of the Australian Wine Export Council (AWEC) offices in London, New York and Frankfurt and help develop new markets including Asia.

With a sliding scale formula, the levy will be 0.25 percent and later 0.20 percent on the first A$10 million of FOB export sales, and 0.15 percent and 0.10 percent on the next A$40 million, with a standard 0.05 percent on remaining sales.

"A small winemaker exporting A$100,000 of wine will pay a levy of just A$250 for the year, whilst the larger companies will probably pay in excess of A$150,000 in the first year," he said in a statement.
The export levy legislation, which was passed last week by the Senate, was an excellent example of government and industry working together, he said. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
